findings.passage: "This bill will make it significantly harder for seniors and vulnerable citizens to vote by mail," said Blackshear.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name after the Senate passed Sub. H.B. 472, which was amended to require photo ID for voting by mail.
subjects: photo ID to vote by mail

findings.passage: H.B. 472 is confusing, entirely unnecessary, and adds hoops for people to jump through just to vote.
findings.note: Same release: his description of the mail-ballot photo ID provisions, which he also says changed a bill meant to help homeless Ohioans get free identifying documents.
subjects: photo ID to vote by mail
free ID documents for people experiencing homelessness

findings.passage: This bill will not protect against voter fraud and creates further uncertainty in our election processes while placing an additional burden on Ohio's election workers and public library employees with another unfunded mandate.
findings.note: Same release: he says the mail-ballot ID rule does not guard against voter fraud and burdens election workers and libraries.
subjects: photo ID to vote by mail

findings.passage: This constitutional amendment is unnecessary and ultimately a distraction from issues that people actually care about,
findings.note: Statement in his name after the Senate passed S.J.R. 10, a proposed constitutional amendment on photo ID to vote. The release also says amendments to widen accepted IDs and provide free state IDs were tabled.
subjects: photo ID at the polls (constitutional amendment)

findings.passage: Photo ID is already required to vote under Ohio law, and this resolution fails to consider key voter protections.
findings.note: Same release: his statement that the photo ID requirement already exists and that the amendment leaves out voter protections.
subjects: photo ID at the polls (constitutional amendment)
